title: Hardware-Assisted Virtualization of Neural Processing Units for Cloud Platforms
problem: Cloud platforms need to virtualize NPUs for multi-tenant ML services while ensuring QoS, but lack system abstraction, architectural, and ISA support for fine-grained dynamic operator scheduling on virtualized NPUs.
motivation: Virtualizing NPUs enables efficient multi-tenant ML service deployment on cloud platforms while maximizing resource utilization and maintaining service quality.
method: Neu10 creates a virtual NPU (vNPU) — a software layer that divides a physical neural processor into slices that can be shared across multiple jobs. It includes a resource allocator that maps these virtual NPUs to physical hardware using pay-as-you-go billing, where each job pays only for the resources it actually uses. It extends the NPU instruction set (the set of operations the processor can execute) to enable dynamic scheduling of individual tensor operations (calculations on multi-dimensional numerical arrays) across multiple virtual NPUs, deciding in real-time which operation runs on which slice.
key_novelty: The core innovation is an NPU instruction set extension that enables fine-grained dynamic scheduling of individual tensor operations (calculations on multi-dimensional arrays) across multiple virtual NPUs in cloud systems.
contributions: vNPU abstraction enabling fine-grained virtualization of heterogeneous compute units in physical NPUs
Resource allocator with pay-as-you-go computing model and flexible virtual-to-physical NPU mappings
ISA extension for fine-grained dynamic tensor operator scheduling across multiple virtual NPUs
limitations: Limitations not discussed in the provided abstract.
primary_theme: NPU virtualization for cloud ML inference
